dossier.public_summary: The dip changes depth between sectors and between odd and even transits and even secondary dips are seen, with one transit almost disappearing to 113 ppm. The size estimate of 3.5 Earth radii falls in a planet-like range but the variable depth and secondary eclipse require a stellar companion. This is best explained as a grazing eclipsing binary, not a planet.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even difference with same sign in all sectors favours an eclipsing binary at twice the period (25.6 d), not a planet at 12.8 d.
Individual transits are wildly inconsistent; the signal is driven by two events on either side of a near non-detection, inconsistent with a stable planet.

Depth changes dramatically between sectors, confirmed by sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source (p_constant 8.778609294459043e-09 within SPOC 2-min). Sector 44 shows essentially no dip.
Secondary eclipse at half orbit with comparable SNR as the brightening is stellar, not planetary; phase_curve amplitude 108.4 ppm also indicates a varying binary companion.

Near-grazing shape (Rstar 0.8063, b 0.9746, radius low) and no clean on_target difference image leave a blended or grazing stellar eclipse as best explanation; size 3.477 Rearth alone does not favour planet.
